html:
The Pacta conventa is an agreement said to have been made in 1102 by which twelve Croatian noble clans accepted King Coloman of Hungary as their king, beginning a union that lasted until 1918.

Coloman was crowned King of Croatia and Dalmatia at Biograd in 1102. The surviving text dates from the 1300s and its authenticity is debated, but its terms match what followed: Croatia kept its nobles' rights, its own diet called the Sabor, and a ban, or viceroy, to govern it. Croatian lawyers later used the pact to argue that Croatia had joined Hungary as a separate kingdom. The union passed to the Habsburgs in 1527 and ended with the creation of Yugoslavia in 1918.
sum: The Pacta conventa is an agreement said to have been made in 1102 by which twelve Croatian noble clans accepted King Coloman of Hungary as their king, beginning a union that lasted until 1918.
